page.introDescription: Connecting Slack gives the CRM a way in and a way out. What it actually does with that is up to you afterwards, one automation at a time.
never: Send anything at all until you build an automation and switch it on
Post anywhere except the destination approved in that automation
Read a direct message between two people
page.connectNote: You approve the workspace in Slack. You can disconnect it here at any time.
page.suggestionsTitle: Afterwards, most teams start with one of these
page.suggestionsDescription: Suggestions, not settings. None of them exist until you pick one and switch it on.

suggestions.title: When a deal is created
suggestions.description: Post the deal to an approved sales channel.

suggestions.title: When a deal is won
suggestions.description: Tell an approved channel that the deal closed.

suggestions.title: When a deal reopens
suggestions.description: Notify one approved channel or teammate.

page.canManageDescription: Here is what Slack gave us. Agents only post where their automation says.
page.cannotManageDescription: Here is what Slack gave us. Only an owner or an admin can disconnect it.
page.agentsDescription: Built in chat, not here. Open one to change it.

page.cannotReachPrivate: Comp AI cannot reach private channels
page.heldBackPermissions: {count, plural, one {Slack held back # permission} other {Slack held back # permissions}}
page.reconnectPrompt: Reconnect to ask again. You lose nothing.

scopeGroups.description: Broad means the whole workspace, not one channel. Open a group to see the details.

errors.userInfoMissing: Slack did not return the installer's profile. Confirm the app has users:read and users:read.email, reinstall it, then try again.

disconnectButton.confirmDescription: Agents stop sending to Slack immediately, and the cached channel list is cleared so a new app re-reads it. Who is matched to which Slack account is kept, so reconnecting the same workspace does not ask you to match everyone again.

channels.joinAskInside: Ask someone inside to invite Comp AI.
channels.readingChannelList: Reading the channel list from Slack.
channels.askSomeoneTitle: Ask someone to add Comp AI

channels.copyFailed: Copying failed. Copy the command above by hand.

people.description: Match your CRM people to Slack once. Agents use these exact accounts later instead of guessing from a similar name.
people.stalled: Comp AI is not reading Slack right now. These matches can be out of date.
people.noneAvailable: No CRM teammates are available to match.
people.footerNote: Refresh after a Slack email changes. The CRM matches exact email addresses only. Someone with no exact match stays unmatched, and an agent stops instead of guessing at a similar name.

reporting.hintRestricted: Only an owner or an admin can change how money is reported.
reporting.saved: Every total is now reported in {currency}.

rates.title: Exchange rates
rates.description: How many {currency} one unit of each currency buys. Fetched daily from open.er-api.com; a rate you enter here wins.
rates.invalidRate: A rate has to be a number greater than zero.

table.searchPlaceholder: Search by name, domain or issuer…
table.empty: No identity provider yet — everyone signs in with Google.

add.redirectHint: Add this at your provider before saving.

copyValue.copyFailed: Could not copy the {label}. Select it instead.

tracking.title: Tracking & Analytics
tracking.description: Track website visitors and automatically add contacts when a form is submitted.

script.title: Tracking script
script.description: One tag, 4 KB, in the head of every page you measure.
script.copyFailedSelect: Could not copy the script. Select it instead.
script.siteIdNote: Site ID {siteId} · Rotating it stops every copy of the old script at once.
script.gtmTab: Add it through Google Tag Manager
script.gtmStep1: In Tag Manager, add a new Custom HTML tag.
script.gtmStep2: Paste this snippet — not the one above — as the tag's HTML.
script.gtmStep3: Trigger it on All Pages, then publish the container. Keep {scriptUrl} off any consent-blocked category you do not need.
script.gtmNote: Tag Manager drops a data-site attribute when it injects a script, so this form carries the site ID in the URL instead.
script.pauseHint: The script keeps loading and records nothing. Your domains and settings are kept
script.rotateDescription: Every copy of the old script stops recording at once, including any you have forgotten about. You will need to paste the new tag on every page that carries the old one. Nothing already collected is lost.
script.pausedToast: Tracking paused. The script stops recording within five minutes.
script.rotatedToast: Site ID rotated. Paste the new tag on your website.

verify.title: Verify installation
verify.description: We load one page and look for the script, then read your Tag Manager container if it is not in the HTML.
verify.pageHint: The page has to be public. A page behind a login always fails this check.
verify.unreachableDescription: {detail} We only follow public pages, and we never follow a redirect to a private address.
verify.missingDescription: The page answered in {ms} ms, but the tag was not in the HTML. Check that it sits in the head, above anything that rewrites the page.
verify.missingContainersNote: We also read Tag Manager container {containers}, and the tag is not in there either.
verify.dropTitle: Tag Manager will drop the site ID
verify.dropDescription: Container {containerId} carries the tag, but the site ID is not in the script URL. Tag Manager keeps only the URL when it injects a script, so a data-site attribute never reaches the page and the tracker never starts. Copy the Tag Manager snippet above and replace the tag's HTML.
verify.dropPageViewNote: A page view did arrive in the last five minutes, so something on this site is still recording.
verify.answeredIn: It answered in {ms} ms. Site ID {siteId} matched, and {allowedClause}.
verify.allowedYes: this domain is on the allow list
verify.allowedNo: this domain is not on the allow list
verify.tagNotInHtmlNote: The tag is not in the HTML, so it only runs once Tag Manager fires it — a page view is the proof.
verify.pageViewArrivedNote: A page view arrived in the last five minutes.
verify.noPageViewYetNote: No page view has arrived yet — open the page in a browser to send one.

domains.title: Allowed domains
domains.description: The script records page views on these hosts only.
domains.empty: Add the domain your website runs on to get your tracking script.

cookies.title: Cookies
cookies.description: How a returning visitor is recognised.

subdomains.label: Limit cookies to subdomains
subdomains.hint: Set the cookie on the exact host that served the page, never on the parent domain

secure.label: Use secure cookies only
secure.hint: Send the cookie over HTTPS and drop it on plain HTTP

dnt.label: Honour Do Not Track
dnt.hint: Record nothing at all when the browser asks not to be tracked

cookies.lifetimeHint: After this a returning visitor counts as somebody new. Shorten it if your policy asks you to.

rules.title: Tracking rules
rules.description: Where the script may run, and how it follows a visitor.

crossDomain.label: Automatic cross-domain linking
crossDomain.hint: Carry the visitor between the domains below, so one journey is not counted as two people

limitToDomains.label: Limit tracking to the domains below
limitToDomains.hint: On any other domain the script loads and then does nothing

sources.title: Traffic sources
sources.description: Where your visitors come from. Only people who have submitted a form are attributed to a record.
sources.empty: No sources yet. They appear once the script records its first page view.
